request.spec:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added grace days. When the sheet's today changes, any open period whose to-date plus the grace days falls before the new today is now closed. All 4 Playwright tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**How it works**
- **Stored setting:** a new migration `V40__sheet_grace_days.sql` adds a `grace_days` column to the sheet. It holds a whole number, is blank when off, and isn't dated.
- **Saving it:** the settings form has a new grace-days field, and the screen shows the value in force (blank means off). Saving it writes `SETTING_CHANGED key=grace-days value=<days>` to the audit file.
- **Changing today:** `SheetService.setToday` now locks the sheet, sets the new today, and then closes the qualifying periods in order of their to-dates. Each one writes `PERIOD_CLOSED ... auto=yes`. The usual rollup lines are written after these.
- **Same close as by hand:** I moved the closing logic into one method, `SheetService.closePeriod`, which both the close button and the automatic close now use. So an automatic close fixes the due-total and writes the audit line exactly as a close by hand does. A close by hand writes the same line as before, without `auto=yes`.

**Decision for you:** an automatic close doesn't check the close permission in the permission matrix. It happens whenever someone allowed to change today changes it (viewers still can't). The request didn't say either way and the tests don't cover it. If an automatic close should only happen when that user could also close the period by hand, it's a one-line check to add.
